title: Color palette with WCAG AA contrast
when: The user wants a color palette, color scheme or theme colors for a page or app, with text that stays readable.
inputs: any color the user already has
prompt:
Goal: A small named palette where every text and background pair in use reaches WCAG AA: 4.5 to 1 for text, 3 to 1 for large text and UI borders.
Steps:
1. Pick roles before hues: background, surface, text, muted text, border, accent, text on accent, success, warning, danger.
2. Choose one accent hue in three shades: a light tint for sections, the base, and a dark shade for accent text.
3. Use near neutrals for the bulk (background around #fafaf9, text around #1c1917) instead of pure black on white.
4. Compute contrast with the WCAG formula (L1 + 0.05) / (L2 + 0.05) for every pair you use; darken the foreground until it passes.
5. Test the primary button label on the accent; if white fails, darken the accent or switch to dark text.
6. Write the palette as custom properties on :root (--color-bg, --color-text, --color-accent) and use only those in rules.
Quality bar:
- One accent plus neutrals and three status colors.
- Muted text passes on both background and surface.
- Meaning never relies on color alone.
Pitfalls:
- Light gray hint text at 2.5 to 1.
- Testing against the page while the text sits on a card surface.
- Brand color as text on a tint of the same hue.
Verify:
- [ ] Each color and background-color pair reaches 4.5 to 1.
- [ ] Rules read var(--color-*) tokens.
- [ ] Links are underlined, not only colored.
- [ ] Pairs and ratios are listed in the reply.
Output: The :root palette and the rules that use it in style.css; the pair and ratio list in the reply.

examples.input: quero uma paleta de cores calma para um site de yoga
examples.output: bg #f7f5f2, text #23201c, accent #2f6b5e with white label at about 6.2 to 1, muted #5c5650
